summary: Stuck model pin after canary throttle suppression causes routing to legacy variant
description:
Issue summary: During a staged canary rollout of pf-3b-v2 for PathFinder Analytics (dedicated pool), a rate-adaptive canary throttle triggered 'suppression' mode which prevented the orchestrator from committing the per-tenant pin. The tenant traffic continued to be routed to the legacy pf-3b-v1 variant, causing inconsistent responses and elevated cost when some requests fell back to the hosted dequantized variant. Impact: customer reports mixed model outputs, degraded quality for ~12% of requests for a critical endpoint and a sudden spike in token usage due to fallback to a higher-cost variant.

Observed window: 2025-02-18 03:05 - 03:50 UTC.

Context: This customer is on a dedicated pool with explicit model version pin requested via API header X-Model-Pin, and a canary rollout (20% weight) was configured with adaptive-rate throttle enabled (adaptive-canary-throttle v2). The edge-proxy applied a transient rate-shed tag which the orchestrator interpreted as a health suppression and did not persist the pin commit in the cluster snapshot.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) On a dedicated tenant with pinned header X-Model-Pin: pf-3b-v2, begin a weighted canary rollout (20%) via console rollout API.
2) Simulate a spike of short-lived concurrent requests to the canary slice to trigger adaptive-canary-throttle thresholds on the edge-proxy.
3) Observe orchestrator logs for pin commit path; confirm whether pin commit RPC returns 202 vs 200.
4) Inspect routing decisions returned by the edge (x-routing-variant header) and compare to requested pin.
5) Verify if snapshot store contains the committed pin entry for the tenant after rollout slice stabilizes.
logs_and_diagnostics: edge-proxy logs (us-east-1) 2025-02-18T03:06:12Z: INFO rate-shed applied: tenant=pf-tenant-88 action=suppress reason=adaptive-throttle threshold=0.2
orchestrator logs 2025-02-18T03:06:15Z: WARN pin-commit-suppressed tenant=pf-tenant-88 snapshot_write_status=skipped reason=health-suppression
serving-runtime logs 2025-02-18T03:06:20Z: DEBUG route-eval tenant=pf-tenant-88 selected_variant=pf-3b-v1 (pin requested pf-3b-v2)
kvcache-metrics: prefix-hit-rate unchanged; no prewarm observed for pf-3b-v2 in tenant pool
investigation_notes: 2025-02-18 04:00 UTC - Triage: Confirmed customer reproduced discrepancy; initial hypothesis: edge suppression flag prevented snapshot commit path.
Checked rollout controller: commit flow returns 'skipped' when health suppression present (code path introduced in adaptive-throttle v2).
Reproduced in internal staging by enabling adaptive-canary-throttle and simulating 200rps spike; observed identical 'pin-commit-suppressed' logs.

Hypothesis refined: edge-proxy annotates requests with suppression metadata which the orchestrator treats as 'abort commit' instead of 'defer commit'. This leaves the tenant in a half-committed state where routing remains bound to previous snapshot epoch.
Temporary mitigation tested: manually forcing a snapshot write via admin endpoint produced a committed entry and restored pinned routing for the tenant.
Risk: If adaptive throttle suppression remains aggressive during low-latency window, automatic commit may never persist leading to rolling inconsistencies across tenants.
comments: Support (Maya Chen) 2025-02-18T05:12Z: Reached out to PathFinder contact (ops@pathfinder.io) to request request IDs and sample traces. Customer confirms ~12% of calls returned different output shape.
Customer (Alex Rivera, PathFinder) 2025-02-18T05:40Z: Provided sample request IDs: req-9832, req-9841, req-9910. They noted risk to production analytics pipeline; asking for ETA on fix.
SRE (Diego Alvarez) 2025-02-18T06:10Z: Confirmed we can force a snapshot commit as a short-term fix. Will coordinate to apply to the dedicated tenant after approval.

Eng (Priya Nair) 2025-02-18T09:30Z: Reproduced locally. Root cause: orchestrator treat_suppressed_as_abort flag default true; change would be to treat suppression as 'defer' and schedule commit after suppression clears. Drafting PR to adjust logic and add metric for suppressed-commits.
Support (Maya Chen) 2025-02-19T14:22Z: Customer approved manual snapshot write at 2025-02-19 15:00 UTC. Applied forced commit; customer confirms traffic now reaches pf-3b-v2 for pinned requests.
Customer (Alex Rivera) 2025-02-19T15:30Z: Verified outputs normalized; thanked team and asked for postmortem and permanent fix timeline.
resolution: Manual snapshot commit applied 2025-02-19 15:00 UTC for tenant pf-tenant-88; pinned routing restored. Engineering merged PR to change suppression handling (orchestrator PR #1223) which treats adaptive-throttle suppression as defer instead of abort and schedules a follow-up commit when suppression clears. Patch scheduled for rollout to prod-us-east on 2025-02-21 during maintenance window.
follow_up_actions: 1) Postmortem doc: create Confluence page documenting root cause, timeline, and customer impact (owner: Priya Nair, due 2025-02-24)
2) Add telemetry: metric suppressed_pin_commits and alert if rate > 1/min for any tenant (owner: SRE team)
3) QA: add regression test to rollout controller simulating adaptive throttle suppression to ensure defer-path commits succeed after suppression clears (owner: rollout-controller team)
4) Customer comms: send summary and offered credit for elevated token cost during incident (owner: CS manager)
5) Monitor: keep a 72-hour watch on pf-tenant-88 routing logs and suppressed-commit metric after patch rollout.
